stories.headline: Goff Wins It Late for THE MACHINES
stories.dek: THE MACHINES 106.08, Lil’ Chops 100.38. 5.7 points in it.
paragraphs: Tight the whole way. Tight like a bad shoe. THE MACHINES were behind this football game until the fourth quarter and won it 106.08 to 100.38, which tells you most of what you need and none of how it felt.

The play that settled it came in the fourth quarter, Sunday night: Jared Goff with an 8-yard touchdown pass. That put THE MACHINES in front at 105.48–100.38, and for all the traffic that had come before it, nobody took it back. There were 12 touchdowns in this game and the one that mattered went THE MACHINES’s way last.

Chris Rodriguez did the heaviest lifting — a 25-yard touchdown run in the second quarter, the Sunday early games, worth 8.5 on its own, though it was Puka Nacua who finished with the biggest number at 18.7. Lamar Jackson and Jared Goff did the rest of the damage. Aaron Rodgers actually outscored every man on the field with 22.0 and still lost, which tells you plenty about the other nine spots.
Somewhere a front office is staring at a bench score and hoping nobody noticed.

stories.headline: Master-Jeti Hold Off Killer Klowns
paragraphs: Not a classic, not a disaster, one of the other ones. Master-Jeti 118.02, Killer Klowns 105.2, a 12.8-point margin that never seriously came under review.

The play that settled it came in the fourth quarter, Sunday night: Jake Bates with a 43-yard field goal. That put Master-Jeti in front at 109.02–105.2, and for all the traffic that had come before it, nobody took it back. There were 10 touchdowns in this game and the one that mattered went Master-Jeti’s way last.

Treylon Burks did the heaviest lifting — a 47-yard touchdown catch in the first quarter, the Sunday early games, worth 10.7 on its own, though it was Kenneth Walker who finished with the biggest number at 29.9. Jake Bates and Seattle Seahawks did the rest of the damage. Kyren Williams answered with 26.7 and it finished 12.8 short.

Killer Klowns will want to look away from this next bit. Keon Coleman sat on their bench and scored 17.6 while Marcus Mariota started and returned 4.4 — 13.2 points in a chair, in a game they lost by 12.8. That is not a defeat, that is a self-inflicted wound with a witness.
Not pretty. They all count the same.

stories.headline: Beaver Eaters Hold Off BIG BLUE
paragraphs: Workmanlike. Businesslike. Several other kinds of like. Beaver Eaters 138.94, BIG BLUE 114.12, a 24.8-point margin that never seriously came under review.

The play that settled it came in the fourth quarter, Sunday night: Bryce Young with a 32-yard touchdown pass. That put Beaver Eaters in front at 118.98–114.12, and for all the traffic that had come before it, nobody took it back. There were 17 touchdowns in this game and the one that mattered went Beaver Eaters’s way last.

Malik Nabers did the heaviest lifting — a 25-yard touchdown catch in the second quarter, the Sunday early games, worth 8.5 on its own, though it was Javonte Williams who finished with the biggest number at 26.3. Bryce Young and Malik Nabers did the rest of the damage. CeeDee Lamb answered with 24.3 and it finished 24.8 short.
Beaver Eaters left Drake Maye and his 26.8 on the bench for Christian Watson, who returned 4.7. It did not matter. It rarely does until the one week it does.
My producer says move on, and for once he is right.

stories.headline: Pork Chop Express Leave No Doubt
stories.dek: Pork Chop Express 100.22, Wookie Leaks 58.62. It was over long before it was finished.
paragraphs: Some games are contests. This was a chore. Pork Chop Express beat Wookie Leaks 100.22 to 58.62, and the 41.6 points between them at the end flatter nobody — Wookie Leaks led early, lost it, and never argued again.

The play that settled it came in the third quarter, the Sunday late games: Jaxon Smith-Njigba with a 28-yard catch. That put Pork Chop Express in front at 43.26–41.62, and for all the traffic that had come before it, nobody took it back. There were 8 touchdowns in this game and the one that mattered went Pork Chop Express’s way last.

Brock Bowers did the heaviest lifting — a 20-yard touchdown catch in the third quarter, the Sunday late games, worth 8.0 on its own, though it was Matt Gay who finished with the biggest number at 16.0. Brock Bowers and James Cook did the rest of the damage. Jacoby Brissett had 11.1 of it for Wookie Leaks. The other nine spots have some explaining to do.
Pork Chop Express left Kyle Monangai and his 27.0 on the bench for Jalen Nailor, who returned 0.0. The result survived it. Their dignity is a separate question.
The good news is that it is over, and that is the whole of the good news.

stories.headline: The Powers of Pain Handle Smoke Dragons
stories.dek: The Powers of Pain 135.8, Smoke Dragons 100.64.
paragraphs: This had the shape of a competitive game without ever being one. The Powers of Pain 135.8, Smoke Dragons 100.64, a 35.2-point margin that never seriously came under review.

They took it in the first quarter — Nico Collins with a 45-yard catch, 13.5–12.6 — and then simply never gave it back. 14 touchdowns were scored after that and not one of them put Smoke Dragons in front again.

Nico Collins led the winners with 23.8, and C.J. Stroud and Brock Purdy kept him company. Bijan Robinson actually outscored every man on the field with 26.7 and still lost, which tells you plenty about the other nine spots.
Smoke Dragons left Brian Robinson and his 24.7 on the bench for Cooper Kupp, who returned 1.3. They won anyway, so it goes in the drawer marked never mind.
Somewhere a waiver claim from August is feeling good about itself.

stories.headline: StillTheCream Survive the Back-and-Forth
stories.dek: StillTheCream 96.9, Guido Haters 78.06. 10 lead changes, and the last one was the only one that kept.
paragraphs: Now this one I enjoyed, and I enjoy almost nothing. StillTheCream and Guido Haters swapped the lead 10 times before one of them finally kept it, and StillTheCream were the ones holding it when the weekend ran out: 96.9–78.06.

They took it in the first quarter — Luther Burden with a 7-yard catch, 14.26–13.96 — and then simply never gave it back. 10 touchdowns were scored after that and not one of them put Guido Haters in front again.

Ka'imi Fairbairn led the winners with 16.0, though Rhamondre Stevenson and Jordan Love did enough that he did not have to do it alone. Emanuel Wilson actually outscored every man on the field with 24.0 and still lost, which tells you plenty about the other nine spots.
Guido Haters left Romeo Doubs and his 17.8 on the bench for Kendre Miller, who returned -0.1. It cost them nothing in the end, which is the best that can be said for it.
I aged a year on that one, and I was already old.

stories.headline: Kamara Wins It Late for n.W.o
stories.dek: n.W.o 85.26, Phins Phag 76.34. 10 lead changes, and the last one was the only one that kept.
paragraphs: My scorekeeper asked to be relieved at halftime. n.W.o and Phins Phag swapped the lead 10 times before one of them finally kept it, and n.W.o were the ones holding it when the weekend ran out: 85.26–76.34.

The play that settled it came in the fourth quarter, Monday night: Alvin Kamara with a 3-yard touchdown run. That put n.W.o in front at 80.56–76.34, and for all the traffic that had come before it, nobody took it back. There were 9 touchdowns in this game and the one that mattered went n.W.o’s way last.

Will Reichard led the winners with 19.0, with Alvin Kamara and Patrick Mahomes close enough behind to matter. Chuba Hubbard actually outscored every man on the field with 24.9 and still lost, which tells you plenty about the other nine spots.
Games like that are why I switched to the second drink. No regrets.

stories.headline: Horsecollars Make It Hurt
stories.dek: Horsecollars 119.6, Gumbas 60.14. It was over long before it was finished.
paragraphs: There is no kind way to file this one. This was a chore. Horsecollars beat Gumbas 119.6 to 60.14, and the 59.5 points between them at the end flatter nobody — Gumbas did not lead at any stage of this football game.
There is no sequence to describe, because there was no sequence. Horsecollars scored first, kept scoring, and the remainder was arithmetic performed in public.

Tetairoa McMillan led the winners with 31.2, though Jonathan Taylor and Zay Flowers did enough that he did not have to do it alone. Tyquan Thornton managed 23.1 for Gumbas, which on an afternoon like this one is a lovely painting in a burning house.
Horsecollars left Isaiah Williams and his 13.3 on the bench for Kalif Raymond, who returned 0.6. No harm done, unless you count the man who had to watch it.
File it, forget it, and let us never speak of it again.
